questions.prompt: Which is NOT a primary function of a hydraulic tank?
options: Allows air to separate and particles to settle
questions.explanation: The tank stores and cools oil and lets air separate and particles settle; the relief valve, not the tank, sets pressure.

questions.prompt: What does the hydraulic pump do?
options: Converts mechanical energy into fluid energy in the form of flow
questions.explanation: The pump creates flow; resistance to flow creates pressure.

questions.prompt: What does the relief valve do?
questions.explanation: The relief (pressure control) valve limits system pressure.

questions.prompt: What does an actuator do?
options: Converts hydraulic energy into mechanical energy to do work
questions.explanation: Cylinders and motors are actuators: they convert hydraulic energy into linear or rotary work.

questions.prompt: In a parallel circuit...
options: Components have equal access to pump flow
Fluid passes through one component and then the next
questions.explanation: In parallel circuits components have equal access to pump flow; in series, fluid passes from one to the next.

questions.prompt: What can result from oil viscosity that is too high?
options: Sluggish operation and extra power required
questions.explanation: High viscosity oil can cause sluggish operation and need more power.

questions.prompt: The cycle time of an actuator depends on...
options: Its displacement (volume) and the flow rate
questions.explanation: Cycle time = displacement divided by flow rate.

questions.prompt: What does Pascal's Law state?
options: A force applied to a confined liquid is transmitted equally in all directions
questions.explanation: Pascal's Law: force on a confined liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.

questions.prompt: The pressure required to lift a load equals...
options: Load force divided by the effective piston area
questions.explanation: Pressure = Force / Area, using the effective piston area.

questions.prompt: What must always be done before servicing a hydraulic system?
options: Remove the tank cap with the engine running
questions.explanation: System pressure must always be relieved before servicing.

questions.prompt: What are the two types of hydraulic tanks?
questions.explanation: Mobile machines use vented or pressurized tanks.

questions.prompt: What do baffle plates in a tank do?
options: Separate the suction and return areas and direct oil flow
questions.explanation: Baffles separate suction and return areas so oil can settle and cool.

questions.prompt: What is the most common type of accumulator on Cat machines?
questions.explanation: The gas-charged accumulator is the most commonly used type.

questions.prompt: Which is one of the four basic functions of accumulators?
questions.explanation: Accumulators compensate for flow variations, maintain pressure, absorb shocks and provide emergency pressure and flow.

questions.prompt: Which filter protects the pump from coarse contaminants?
questions.explanation: A suction filter protects pumps from coarse contaminants.

questions.prompt: Why are most cartridge and canister filters fitted with bypass valves?
options: To ensure system flow is never blocked
questions.explanation: The bypass valve keeps flow going if the filter clogs, though the oil is then unfiltered.

questions.prompt: Which is an indicator of filter failure?
options: Dirty oil and accelerated valve wear
questions.explanation: Dirty oil, accelerated valve wear, a noisy pump or a bypass alarm point to filter failure.

questions.prompt: Which two types of oil coolers are used on Cat machines?
questions.explanation: Cat machines use air-to-oil and water-to-oil coolers.

questions.prompt: What are the four primary causes of pump or motor failure?
questions.explanation: The four primary causes are cavitation, aeration, contamination and improper fluid.

questions.prompt: What causes cavitation?
options: Too much oil in the tank
Air leaks on the pressure side
The pump receiving little or no oil, so vapour cavities form and collapse
questions.explanation: When the pump is starved, vapour cavities form and collapse, damaging metal surfaces.

questions.prompt: What is aeration?
options: Air entrapped in the oil, caused by air leaks in the system
questions.explanation: Aeration is entrapped air from leaks; both aeration and cavitation give a rattling sound.

questions.prompt: How do hydraulic motors compare with hydraulic pumps?
options: They are nearly identical in construction
questions.explanation: Hydraulic motors are nearly identical to pumps but convert hydraulic energy into rotary motion.

questions.prompt: When are hydraulic hoses used instead of tubes?
options: When components move in relation to each other
questions.explanation: Hoses are used where flexibility is needed; tubes are rigid steel lines.

questions.prompt: Which repair options apply to a leaking connection?
options: Retorque, replace seals or replace the connector
questions.explanation: For leaking connections: retorque, replace seals or replace the connector.

questions.prompt: What are the three general categories of hydraulic valves?
questions.explanation: Valves are grouped as directional control, flow control and pressure control.

questions.prompt: What does a make-up valve do?
options: Lets return oil flow to the actuator line when return pressure exceeds actuator line pressure, preventing cavitation
questions.explanation: A make-up valve is a check valve that refills the actuator line, e.g. when a load drops faster than pump flow.

questions.prompt: What does a flow control valve typically do?
options: Regulates actuator speed or divides flow between circuits
questions.explanation: Flow control valves regulate actuator speed or divide flow.

questions.prompt: When is a pressure reducing valve used?
options: When circuit pressure requirements are less than supply pressure
questions.explanation: Pressure reducing valves supply a lower pressure to a circuit than the supply pressure.

questions.prompt: What does the rod wiper seal do?
options: Seals the head to the tube
Seals the piston to the tube
Keeps dirt from entering the cylinder
questions.explanation: The rod wiper keeps dirt out as the rod retracts.

questions.prompt: What is a single acting cylinder?
options: A cylinder hydraulically powered in only one direction
A cylinder with rods on both ends
A cylinder powered in both directions
questions.explanation: A single acting cylinder is powered one way; a double acting cylinder is powered both ways.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a snubber in a cylinder?
options: To slow the rod near the end of its stroke and protect the cylinder
questions.explanation: The snubber enters a small bore near the end of the stroke, restricting flow and cushioning the stop.
